items.question: How are QR codes generated entirely in the browser?
items.answer: We use client-side JavaScript QR matrix encoding to generate canvas and SVG graphics directly in your browser. Your URLs, text, or contact data are never sent to external generator APIs.

items.question: What do the error correction levels (L, M, Q, H) mean?
items.answer: Error correction allows QR codes to be scanned even if partially obscured or damaged: Level L recovers ~7% of data, Level M recovers ~15%, Level Q recovers ~25%, and Level H recovers ~30%. Level M is recommended for general use.

items.question: Why does the tool show a contrast warning?
items.answer: Optical QR scanners rely on strong contrast between dark modules and a light background. Low contrast (ratio < 4.5:1) or inverted colors (white code on dark background) often fail on older phone cameras and handheld barcode scanners.

items.question: Should I download PNG or SVG format?
items.answer: PNG is ideal for digital screens, websites, and emails. SVG is an infinitely scalable vector format essential for high-resolution print materials, signs, stickers, and billboards without pixelation.

items.question: What content types can I encode?
items.answer: You can generate QR codes for Website URLs, Plain Text, Email addresses, Phone numbers, SMS messages, and digital vCard contact cards.

items.question: Do these QR codes ever expire?
items.answer: No. These are static, direct-payload QR codes. Unlike subscription-based QR services, there is no redirect server or middleman. The code points permanently to your entered URL or text.

items.question: Is any of my encoded data saved or uploaded?
items.answer: No. Everything is rendered locally inside your browser DOM. No data is stored, tracked, or transmitted.

items.question: What is the minimum recommended print size for a QR code?
items.answer: For standard mobile scanning at arm’s length, print QR codes at least 2 × 2 cm (0.8 × 0.8 inches) with at least 4 modules of quiet zone border margin.
